source.title: Deep Exploration of Epoch-wise Double Descent in Noisy Data: Signal Separation, Large Activation, and Benign Overfitting
source.authors: Tomoki Kubo; Ryuken Uda; Yusuke Iida

record.tranche_reason: Tests epoch-wise delayed re-generalization on noisy CIFAR-10, an image-classification setting rather than a small algorithmic dataset.
record.gate_note: The study reports its own test-loss trajectories and training fit, so these are rows for V3. Its internal-signal and large-activation analyses are reported results relevant to its proposed account of delayed generalization, but they do not measure the circuit formation, memorization-component removal, or progress-measure prediction specified by V2; they are recorded under fits_no_version. Background results attributed to other studies are not included.
record.test_reason: The study measures epoch-wise double descent under 30% label noise on CIFAR-10 with MLPs, not grokking. In MLP7, test loss first falls while clean data are learned (1–100 epochs), rises while noisy labels are memorized, then falls again after about 7,000 epochs. Test performance never sits near chance waiting for a late jump. Grokking is mentioned only in the introduction, through cited work (Power, Humayun, Li, Liu, Davies). The only measure is test loss, reported in words, and no initialization scale or weight norm is varied. So no result bears on V3 as stated (grokking-like delay switched by the training regime) or on any other version. The re-generalization result is a related but different construct and is recorded under fits_no_version. This call is borderline: if double descent is treated as a grokking-like delay (as in Davies et al.), r1–r3 would be a T3 test of V3 that supports it in MLP7 only.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that epoch-wise double descent with noisy data corresponds to benign overfitting: only MLP7 re-generalizes after fitting the noisy labels. They propose a scenario in which clean/noisy signal separation in outer layers and a shallow large activation compress input patterns, letting the rest of the network fit the noise. They make no claim about grokking.
record.recipe_differences: Uses noisy CIFAR-10 image classification and fully connected MLPs, rather than small algorithmic datasets and the original grokking setup. The study investigates epoch-wise double descent and internal activations.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported test-loss outcome varies by architecture: MLP7 shows double descent, MLP5 does not show an increase in test loss, and MLP3 shows increased test loss without double descent. Signal separation is weaker in MLP3 than in MLP7 and MLP5.

fits_no_version.finding: MLP7 on CIFAR-10 with 30% label noise shows epoch-wise double descent: test loss rises from about 100 to 7,000 epochs, then falls after fitting the noisy labels. MLP5 and MLP3 do not re-generalize despite a comparable fit to the training data.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Epoch-wise double descent (re-generalization after noisy-label memorization) in image MLPs depends on model size and depth.

fits_no_version.finding: Hidden activations for clean and noisy training data separate over training, more strongly in deeper layers; separation is weaker in MLP3.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Clean/noisy internal signal separation accompanies noisy-label memorization in noisy CIFAR-10 MLPs.

fits_no_version.finding: A single large activation emerges in a shallow layer in all three models. In MLP7 its onset coincides with double descent at about 7,000 epochs, and its magnitude tracks input class rather than the noisy label.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Shallow-layer massive activations emerge during re-generalization in noisy-label training.

record.problems: The principal delayed-generalization result is reported for MLP7 only; MLP5 and MLP3 do not show the same pattern. The core test-loss outcomes are described qualitatively, without numerical values or uncertainty estimates in the text. The study tests one image dataset and one label-noise level, and does not vary initialization or weight norm.

untested.parts: No algorithmic datasets, no chance-to-near-perfect accuracy jump, no variation of training-set size.
No circuit analysis or progress measures. The activation-separation and large-activation analyses concern double descent, not grokking circuits.
No grokking-like delay from a chance-level start is measured. Initialization scale and weight norm are not varied. No text or molecule data.
No weight decay, no critical dataset size, no ungrokking.
No comparison of the algorithms learned across runs.
Adam is used throughout with no optimizer or numerical control, so artifact explanations are not tested.

record.verdict_notes: All models were trained with Adam at learning rate 1e-5, without weight decay or any reported regularization. Test-loss outcomes are given only qualitatively. Each model appears to have a single run, with no seeds or uncertainty reported for the loss curves. The reader's V3 labels (supports for MLP7, limits_scope for MLP5/MLP3) are withdrawn because the construct does not match V3.

versions.untested_parts: No small algorithmic dataset, training-set-size comparison, or chance-to-near-perfect test-accuracy trajectory is tested.

The study analyzes clean/noisy activation separation and large activations, but does not test formation of a generalizing algorithmic circuit, later removal of memorizing components, or whether continuous progress measures anticipate a test-accuracy jump.

Tests noisy CIFAR-10 image classification with three MLP architectures. Does not vary initialization scale or weight norm, test text or molecules, or establish that those settings switch the delay on or off.
No weight-decay or low-norm intervention, critical dataset-size test, or ungrokking test.
Does not identify or compare algorithms learned across runs.
Does not test adaptive-optimizer instability or floating-point/softmax explanations by controlling them.

rows.subject: MLP7
rows.size_stated: Six hidden layers with 2048, 2048, 1024, 1024, 512, and 512 neurons; output layer with 10 neurons
rows.operation_detail: Measured test-loss trajectory during training on CIFAR-10 with 30% training-label noise.
rows.baseline: Test loss increased during the overfitting phase before the double-descent phase.
rows.value: Test loss began decreasing after around 7,000 epochs; the paper says this occurred after the model fitted both clean and noisy training data well.
rows.note: The reported outcome is a test-loss decrease, not an exact test-accuracy value. The paper says the model fit both clean and noisy training data well.
rows.check: This is epoch-wise double descent: test loss rises during noisy-label memorization, then falls after about 7,000 epochs. Early test performance is not near chance, so it is not the grokking-like delay V3 names. Values are qualitative, read from Fig. 1.

source_check.correct: MLP7 test loss decreases again after approximately 7,000 epochs. For grokking claim versions, state=cannot_determine; versions=none.
source_check.problem: Observed describes epoch-wise double descent; it does not establish a grokking claim version.

relation.reason: The introduction discusses grokking and proposed connections with double descent, without an empirical grokking test.

tranche.reason: The experiments investigate noisy-data double descent and its internal correlates; they neither test nor use any listed grokking claim version.

source_check.notes: The descriptive results are supported, but their states concern other phenomena; with versions=none they cannot establish grokking states. The proposed compression/subnetwork mechanism is an interpretation rather than a demonstrated causal mechanism.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: MLP7 on CIFAR-10 with 30% training-label noise
reader_labels.reason: Test loss decreased after around 7,000 epochs following an overfitting phase, while the model had fitted clean and noisy training data well (r1).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: MLP5 and MLP3 on CIFAR-10 with 30% training-label noise
reader_labels.reason: The delayed re-generalization pattern was not reported for these models: MLP5 did not show increased test loss, and MLP3's test loss increased without double descent (r2, r3).
